cells.tense: Right now you can see the way through and you keep the room level while you do it.
cells.act: build the first new thing from what the clearing showed
cells.ask: Take what you already worked out and make the first rough version of it — draft it, assemble it, start the real thing — done enough that it exists.
cells.core: You can see the shape of a thing before the room can, and you keep it fair while you say it. Nothing gets tilted just because you got there first. People find their footing around you and often don't notice it was you who set it. That is the good version of this — the clear end held steady for whoever is still walking toward it. Now something new is standing on that cleared ground, and it only needs making. Take what you already worked out and build the first version — not the plan for it, the thing itself, done roughly. Draft it, assemble it, start the real thing in whatever form it takes. Get it far enough that it exists. Calibrated means it is here, not that it is ready for review.

cells.verb: charting the passage and keeping it even

cells.tense: The route you are steering is already several turns beyond where the road now goes.
cells.act: engage the hard part on purpose and see what holds
cells.ask: Go straight at the part you have been routing around — one real attempt, no rehearsal — and watch what holds up under your own hands.
cells.core: Where you direct things, the work runs past the day. You have the whole crossing laid out in your head — the turns, the snags, the fix for each — and you are bracing against a stretch nobody has reached yet. The mind is doing its job. It is just doing it somewhere the body has not arrived, so the attention gets spent on the office instead of the river. There is a fix here that is not less care. Aim the care at the actual difficulty and find out what is real by touching it. Take the one part you have been working around and meet it head-on. You will lose some of the version you were carrying. What answers your hands is what you can actually build on, and it will tell you more in an hour than the planning has in a month.

cells.tense: For some time you have been standing past the fair act you already knew to take.
cells.act: return the small thing you owe before anyone asks
cells.ask: Settle the oldest thing you owe someone — a reply, a borrowed item, a few dollars — before they have to bring it up.
cells.core: Where you keep things even, the ledger has a line sitting open. You still see what is fair — that part has not gone — but noticing has stopped turning into anything done. The scale reads fine in your head. Nothing outside it has moved. Open items have piled up, and the piling is what has you standing here. The motion back is smaller than it feels. Choose the oldest open item and close it out before anyone has to ask. A reply. A thing returned. A few dollars where they belong. You are not settling a case or proving a point. You are putting the pen down on one line, and the next one gets easier once your hand remembers the motion.
cells.sheetLine: You still see what is fair, and it no longer reaches anyone.

cells.tense: You have been charting the course for the room and calling it just how things run.
cells.act: let the vision be shared with one other
cells.ask: Walk one person through the whole picture this week — the way you actually hold it — so it stops living only inside your head.
cells.core: You are better at finding a way through than anyone around you says out loud, including you. The whole thing works — the timing, the leveling, the quiet steering — and your account of it is that it is not a skill, just what you happen to do. What you do is carry the route in your head, and nobody else gets to see it. What sits under that is not modesty. The picture got separated from its own name, and it goes back together by being handed to one person — the vision shown, not performed. Take the way you see it and put it into someone else's hands, spoken plainly. Then you find out what you have been doing.
cells.sheetLine: The room leans on your steering, and you wave it off as nothing.
cells.verb: charting the passage and keeping it even
